name: DNA Grammar Artifacts
description: Placeable wrappers for the live-renderable grammars in /dna. Each one packages a research-render's build code as a registered artifact: the same Sim.build(cfg) call, wrapped in a Node3D scene. Promotes lsystem, pattern, rd, trajectory findings from gallery-only to placeable in any map.
theoreticalGrounding: Federated rendering: each grammar's existing build function becomes a placeable artifact. The 'wrapper' is per-grammar, not central — same architectural commitment as facade_builder.

lsystem_artifact.name: L-System Artifact
lsystem_artifact.description: Placeable lsystem-grammar wrapper. Reads a JSON config (axiom, rules, iterations, walk params, colors) and renders branching tubes via LSystemSim.rewrite + LSystemTurtle.walk + LSystemTurtle.to_tubes. Same build path as render_lsystem.gd and dna_workstation.
lsystem_artifact.qfep_connection: F_order: the rewrite rule applied iteratively until structure emerges.

dna.default: group=unset - _ready() still returns before building anything when neither a config_path nor a group is named, which is what every existing placement is: 10 bare `pattern_artifact` tokens across 6 maps (Symmetry_Group, Track_Symmetry x2, Trial_gate10_21, Trial_gate8_sym_size x2, Trial_gate8_sym_type x2, Trial_gate8_sym_typeM x2), not one of them passing a config. They render nothing today and render nothing after this change - byte for byte the same empty floor slot. apply_grid_config now returns without rebuilding unless a key it recognises arrived, ignores a group name that is not in the list rather than assigning it, and never rebuilds before _ready has built once (it used to _clear() and _build() unconditionally, which would have double-built any placement that ever did pass a config).
dna.was: no axis, and the seventeen groups one function call away. Every parameter came from a JSON file named by config_path, and config_path defaults to empty - so a map token could name this artifact but could never name a group, and PatternSim.GROUPS, the closed set of seventeen this artifact exists to display, was unreachable from map data entirely. The ten placed tokens are the proof: all bare, so all silent. An invisible artifact holding a 2x2 floor slot in six maps.
dna.note: group is DERIVED, not transcribed: the eighteen values are PatternSim.GROUPS in PatternSim's own IUC order with `unset` prepended, and PatternSim.group_enum() is the code that resolves each name. The seventeen are a CLOSED set - Fedorov: exactly seventeen ways a pattern can repeat in the plane, no eighteenth - so naming one is not a style choice, it is the whole claim a tile makes about which symmetries it obeys. `unset` is the eighteenth value and it is not a group: it is the shipped silence, declared because the export default has to be inside the declared list (the gate fails a default that is not) and because it is the state every map is actually in. When a group is named without a config the artifact builds from DEFAULT_DNA - PatternSim's own defaults (tile 32, seed 7, bauhaus, canvas 512) with one departure the staged corpus already made, a dot motif at radius 0.38 rather than a random one, because a random motif at density 0.5 buries the symmetry in noise and the symmetry is the only thing this axis is about.
dna.measurement_risk: READ THIS BEFORE BELIEVING A VERDICT. Without the fixture, the default frame renders NOTHING - the axis's own default is the blank state - and a blank against seventeen patterns would score an enormous bite that is a fact about an empty room. So dna.fixture supplies a tracked staged config (pt03_p4m_alhambra: dot motif, seed 3, alhambra palette, tile 32) and the sweep becomes a controlled experiment in which only the group varies. Two consequences to expect and not misread: (a) the `unset` and `p4m` frames are IDENTICAL by construction, because pt03's own group is p4m and unset means 'let the config decide'; (b) the neighbouring groups are genuinely close pictures - p3 against p31m, p4 against p4g - so a faint pair there is the mathematics, not a dead axis. Check p1 against p6m first, which is bare translation against six-fold rotation with mirrors.
dna.declined: palette (8 named palettes in PatternSim.PALETTES). It would be the strongest-biting and emptiest axis available: it repaints every pixel and says nothing about symmetry, which is a colour swatch, not an argument. Also declined: motif (random | dot), which is real - whether the group's symmetry is legible depends on the repeating unit having a form - but it is two-valued and it is a fact about the thing the group ACTS ON, so in one frame the two would fight and the critic would measure the collision. tile_size, canvas_size and quad_size are sizes.

pattern_artifact.name: Pattern Artifact
pattern_artifact.description: Placeable wallpaper-pattern wrapper. Reads a JSON config (group, motif_seed, palette, tile_size) and renders the resulting pattern as a textured quad facing up — readable as floor tile, banner, or table-top.
pattern_artifact.qfep_connection: F_order: 17 wallpaper groups as the algebraic vocabulary of repetition.

rd_artifact.name: Reaction-Diffusion Artifact
rd_artifact.description: Placeable Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion wrapper. Simulates the chemical field per config (F, K, iterations, grid_size, seed) and renders the result as a colored heightmap mesh. Spots, stripes, mazes, coral, mitosis, chaos — the full Turing zoo.
rd_artifact.qfep_connection: lambda_edge: two chemicals at the boundary of reaction and diffusion produce all of pattern emergence.

mesh_grammar_artifact.name: Mesh Grammar Artifact
mesh_grammar_artifact.description: Placeable mesh-grammar wrapper. Reads a JSON config (seed type, generations, list of rules with selectors and params) and builds the resulting procedural mesh via MeshGrammarNode. Supports basic seeds (cube/sphere/icosahedron) and the standard ops (extrude, inset, bulge, scallop, petal_splay, scatter, etc.). DNA-bridged seeds (CA/RD/L-system) are skipped — those configs fall back to image_billboard.
mesh_grammar_artifact.qfep_connection: F_order: face-rewriting rules applied iteratively until form emerges from a primitive seed.

trajectory_artifact.name: Trajectory Artifact
trajectory_artifact.description: Placeable force-trajectory wrapper. Integrates the configured force system (Lorenz, three-body, double pendulum, etc.) and renders the resulting trails as a single MultiMesh of cylinder segments, colored start→end. Time becomes a spatial axis; chaos becomes sculptural.
trajectory_artifact.qfep_connection: F_order + E_entropy: deterministic forces integrated produce structures that read as chaos.
